\section{NVE Threshold Sensitivity Analysis}
\label{sec:appendix_sensitivity}

We report the full sensitivity analysis for the NVE diagnostic framework introduced in Section~\ref{sec:results}. The main text reports Task~B2 (any CIVO detection, $\nve \geq 1.5\times$). Here we additionally present Task~B1, which restricts the positive class to \emph{sustained} CIVO---experiments exhibiting persistent, accelerating value overestimation that progresses to performance collapse. Transient CIVO cases (e.g., exp~009b, which self-corrects after a brief excursion above the threshold) are classified as negative in B1.

\subsection{Per-Experiment NVE Values}

Table~\ref{tab:nve_raw} lists the NVE values at 35K+ training steps for all eight factorial experiments. Experiments are sorted by descending NVE. Experiment 008e\_v3\_s2 exhibits elevated NVE ($3.78\times$) due to Imagination-Reality Divergence (IRD), a mechanistically distinct phenomenon from CIVO, and is classified as negative in both tasks.

input.old_string: The four conditions capture complementary signals: (1)~\emph{Magnitude} ($r_t \geq 0.49$) confirms that value predictions have reached at least 49\% of evaluation return; (2)~\emph{Velocity} ($\Delta r_t > 0.1$) rules out slow drift or plateau behavior; (3)~\emph{Acceleration} ($\Delta r_t > \Delta r_{t-1}$, both $> 0.1$) filters oscillatory paths where the ratio rises and falls without sustained divergence; (4)~\emph{Evaluation decline} ($\geq 2$ of 3 recent checkpoints decline) confirms that overestimation coincides with actual performance degradation. A majority threshold (2 of 3) provides robustness against single-checkpoint evaluation noise while remaining sensitive to sustained decline; requiring 3/3 declines risks missing gradual onset, while a longer window (e.g., 2 of 5) would delay detection by two checkpoint intervals for rapid collapses. Sensitivity analysis over $\tau_\text{mag} \in [0.30, 0.70]$ confirms that $\tau_\text{mag} = 0.49$ maximizes Youden's $J = 0.714$; raising the threshold to $0.50$ loses one true positive (seed~3 triggers at $r_t = 0.497$) with no reduction in false positives, since both false alarms have $r_t > 0.70$ at trigger time and cannot be separated by magnitude alone. The velocity threshold $\tau_\text{vel} = 0.1$ is similarly stable: TPR remains $3/3$ for $\tau_\text{vel} \in [0.05, 0.18]$, and raising $\tau_\text{vel}$ to $0.15$ eliminates both false positives (whose acceleration values fall below the stricter threshold) while retaining all true positives. We retain the more permissive $\tau_\text{vel} = 0.1$ to avoid overfitting to $n{=}10$ runs.

+Sensitivity analysis over $\tau_\text{mag} \in [0.30, 0.70]$ confirms that $\tau_\text{mag} = 0.49$ maximizes Youden's $J = 0.714$; raising the threshold to $0.50$ loses one true positive (seed~3 triggers at $r_t = 0.497$) with no reduction in false positives, since both false alarms have $r_t > 0.70$ at trigger time. The velocity threshold $\tau_\text{vel} = 0.1$ is stable across $[0.05, 0.18]$ (TPR remains $3/3$); we retain $0.1$ to avoid overfitting to $n{=}10$ runs.
\paragraph{Validation.}

We apply the detector retrospectively to ten runs spanning three conditions: trained duration embedding (CIVO-positive, $n{=}3$), untrained or absent embedding (CIVO-negative, $n{=}3$), and vanilla baselines ($n{=}4$). Ground truth labels derive from manual inspection: a run is CIVO-positive if it exhibits sustained $\nve \geq 1.5\times$ with subsequent evaluation collapse. Table~\ref{tab:detector-validation} reports all results.

In practice, alerts before 70K steps can be treated as high-confidence CIVO indicators; later alerts warrant manual inspection.
\paragraph{Limitations.}

Four constraints bound the current detector. First, the three-checkpoint window cannot distinguish transient dips from sustained collapse (the source of the 009a false alarm). Second, the acceleration condition assumes monotonically increasing overestimation during onset; oscillatory trajectories that eventually collapse could evade detection until acceleration stabilizes. Third, the detector identifies a \emph{pattern} (rising value-evaluation ratio with declining performance) rather than a \emph{mechanism}: run 009c shows that non-CIVO pathologies produce the same signature. Fourth, threshold values ($\tau_\text{mag} = 0.49$, $\tau_\text{vel} = 0.1$) were calibrated on ten runs across two environments; generalization to different reward scales requires further validation.
